name: San Juan Worm
imitates: A red bloodworm or aquatic worm; one of the simplest and most productive nymphs for trout in rivers and still water.

steps.text: Slide a countersunk bead over the hook point, small hole first, up to the eye.
Seat the hook in the vise, slide the bead back, and start the thread behind the eye with a few locking wraps.
Set the bead mid-shank and build thread dams on both sides of it, crossing over a few times so it cannot spin or slide.
Flatten the thread by spinning it, then lay touching wraps back to the rear of the hook.
Lay about 1.5 inches of chenille on top of the shank with roughly half an inch hanging off the back, and tie it in at the rear.
Advance the thread to the back of the bead, fold the forward section of chenille over, and wrap it down firmly.
Cross the thread to the front of the bead, fold the chenille over the bead and secure it with a few wraps, then add locking wraps in front.
Advance the thread leaving a small gap behind the eye and tie the chenille down so the front tail matches the rear one in length.
Pull the front chenille back, form a neat head, and whip finish twice.
Seal the exposed thread with a bodkin and head cement or nail hardener, then trim both chenille ends to length. The finished fly.
